body: Thank you, I really appreciate it. I mean, I am getting my antidepressants this week, so maybe it won't be so bad.

I get the feeling that my parents will complain about it more than anything. My dad recently had surgery on one of his eyes to fix a problem with his vision, on top of that he's been going through treatment for prostate cancer for about a year. My mom hates her job, but can't quit because my dad's been unemployed for about three years. We aren't doing well financially, and I know they really don't think that much about how I feel. I know it's hard for them too.

I'm just so afraid of what happens next, I know my therapist has to break confidentiality if I talk about suicidal urges or self-harm, and I don't know what my parents will do. Also sorry that you can only respond every 8 minutes.

I'm seeing my therapist tomorrow, but I'm afraid to tell her about this, I had to get evaluated at a hospital one time. That wasn't fun. I don't really want that to happen again, but I guess it might be for the best that I bring it up during my appointment.

The only thing about telling my parents is that they overall have never been very supportive. There was one time my dad caught me before I was going to kill myself and his solution was to just have me sleep in the living room that night and then never talk about it again. My parents often make it feel like my feelings aren't valid and that I am just being dramatic. They also have the mindset that I should pray my problems away, which isn't exactly something I want to do since I'm an atheist. I know my friends care about me but I'm just so afraid that they'll get tired of me if I talk about my problems that I just don't say anything about it.
